title: Navigation API: `abort the ongoing navigation` never gets called with DOMException?
body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

As title suggests [abort-the-ongoing-navigation](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/nav-history-apis.html#abort-the-ongoing-navigation) states that:

"To abort the ongoing navigation given a [Navigation](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/nav-history-apis.html#navigation) navigation and an optional [DOMException](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException) error:"

There does not seem to be any spec algorithms that calls this, with an actual exception value, which means that step 5 always is true. This problem arose while testing these features in Gecko in [this test](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/source/testing/web-platform/tests/navigation-api/navigate-event/navigation-back-same-document-preventDefault.html#23) - since there's no javascript running, the exception will not have any stack frame information to be extracted in [step 3 of abort-a-navigateevent](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/nav-history-apis.html#abort-a-navigateevent).

This should probably be enough reason to remove the `DOMException` as optional value from the algorithm and have the extract information step be different in the `abort-a-navigateevent` (to be able to provide `.filename` property)? 

cc @farre
